body.statement:
The canonical encoder orbit \([g_\theta]_{\mathfrak S_n\ltimes\operatorname {Isom}(\mathbb T)^n}\) is invariant under every coordinatewise circular latent reparameterization, including orientation reversal.  Moreover \(d_Q\) is an intrinsic symmetric orbit distance, and on the bounded model class
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta).
\]
body.proof_tex:
For one coordinate let \(x'=\psi(x)\), where \(\psi\) is any circle diffeomorphism.  Let \(q^0d\lambda\) and \(q^{0\prime}d\lambda\) be the same baseline law, and let \(\beta,\beta'\) be the two probability-integral gauges.  Both \(\beta\) and \(\beta'\circ\psi\) push \(q^0d\lambda\) to \(\lambda\).  Hence
\[
 I=(\beta'\circ\psi)\circ\beta^{-1}
\tag{1}
\]
preserves \(\lambda\).  Thus \(|I'|=1\), its derivative has constant sign, and \(I(t)=t+c\) or \(I(t)=-t+c\) modulo \(2\pi\).  Since \(h'=\psi\circ h\),
\[
 g'=\beta'\circ h'=I\circ\beta\circ h=I\circ g.
\tag{2}
\]
Applying (2) coordinatewise and allowing one common permutation proves invariance.

The finite permutation group and the compact circle-isometry group act isometrically on \(L^2(\lambda^n;\mathbb T^n)\).  Inversion gives symmetry, composition plus Minkowski gives the triangle inequality, and compactness makes the infimum attained.

For a canonical alignment define
\[
 \phi_i=\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\circ I_i\circ\beta_{\widetilde\theta,\pi(i)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Integrating the positive perfect-intervention density over the coordinates other than \(i\) gives its \(i\)-th marginal \(q_i^0\).  The density bounds therefore give class-uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(q_i^0\), hence a class-uniform Lipschitz bound for \(\beta_{\theta i}^{-1}\).  They and decoder conditioning also bound the density of \(\bar P_\theta\) relative to \(\lambda^n\).  Applying these bounds to the two auxiliary directed losses and taking infima proves
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq C d_Q(\theta,\widetilde\theta).
\tag{4}
\]
This is only a one-way comparison and does not characterize the zero set of the auxiliary discrepancy.
